paragraphs: Friend, the disciples came asking who gets to be the greatest, and Jesus didn't hand them a ranking. He stood a little child among them and said, "unless you change and become like little children, you will never enter the kingdom of heaven" (Matthew 18:3). Then He said, "whoever humbles himself like this little child is the greatest in the kingdom of heaven" (Matthew 18:4). So the way up in this kingdom is DOWN, and I'll be honest, I've been trying to climb it the wrong direction my whole life.

Here's the heart of it, baker. Little ones matter to God, and they matter so much that Jesus gets serious about anyone who causes one to stumble, and about sin in our own lives (Matthew 18:6-9). He says, "See that you do not look down on any of these little ones" (Matthew 18:10). Then He tells of a man who leaves ninety-nine sheep to search for the one that strayed, and He says, "your Father in heaven is not willing that any of these little ones should perish" (Matthew 18:14). I think that's the part to hold onto, because the Father goes after the one who's wandered off.

That same heart shows up when someone sins against you. Jesus says to go to him privately, and if he listens, "you have won your brother over" (Matthew 18:15), so the goal is winning your brother, never winning the argument. So stay humble, stay close to the little ones, and keep going after your brother, and hold onto Jesus' promise: "where two or three gather together in My name, there am I with them" (Matthew 18:20). And friend, His teaching isn't over yet.
